hints.title: Palindrome Parity Condition
hints.text: A set of characters can form a palindrome if at most one character appears an odd number of times.

hints.title: Bitmask Representation
hints.text: Represent character frequency parity using a 26-bit mask, where bit i denotes odd parity for character i.

hints.title: Prefix Path XOR
hints.text: The path mask between u and v is mask[u] ^ mask[v]. Valid pairs have bitwise differences equal to 0 or a single power of 2.

hints.title: Implementation

variables: n: number of nodes in tree
complexity.notes: Bitmask representation of character frequencies with prefix XOR frequency counting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Traversing every pair of tree nodes takes O(n^2) which is far too slow for n up to 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(26 * n) time using a bitmask hash map and O(n) space for tree storage.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use the property that LCA parity cancels out to reduce tree path queries to root-prefix XOR matching.
